title: GPU sandbox profiles: deterministic tenant throttles and graceful capacity reclamation
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a new GPU sandbox profile system that enforces deterministic per-tenant token-throughput contracts while providing a graceful capacity reclamation path when demand exceeds reserved capacity. This ticket covers the runtime admission controller changes, cgroup/QoS mappings, quota reconciliation service, and autoscaler integration necessary for predictable throughput guarantees on Dedicated capacity.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Sandbox profiles can be created and assigned to tenants via the Dedicated API and Console (API contract + Console form).
2) When a tenant is assigned a sandbox profile, the runtime enforces a steady-state token throughput cap with sub-100ms admission decision latency 99% of the time.

3) During temporary surge above reserved capacity, the system applies a configurable graceful reclamation policy (soft-throttle -> capped queue -> short-lived preemption) and never hard-preempts running in-progress requests unless >30s over-contract.
4) Quota reconciliation service reports daily drift between committed throughput and actual usage and emits alerts when drift > 5% for 24h.
5) End-to-end e2e tests covering steady-state enforcement, surge reclamation, and autoscaler-triggered expansion pass in CI and on staging cluster.

Testing: unit tests for admission logic, k8s integration tests for cgroup mapping, and chaos tests for noisy neighbor injection.

design_decisions: Deterministic enforcement uses a token-bucket per-tenant with tokens consumed proportional to expected per-token GPU time rather than raw token count — this maps throughput more closely to device time across heterogeneous models.

Three-stage graceful reclamation chosen to prioritize availability for in-flight requests: 1) soft-throttle (response delay hints), 2) bounded queue with latency SLO gate, 3) short-lived preemption only when queue > configured threshold for >30s.
We will prefer conservative autoscaler signals (headroom + sustained queue length) to avoid flip-flopping; aggressive scaling only if headroom deficit persists for >2 minutes.
Mapping sandbox profiles to cgroup v2 annotations keeps enforcement at OS level and allows infra to leverage existing node-level QoS without kernel patches.
To avoid tenant starvation during scale-down, we implement a reconciliation window and prioritized draining that respects express SLA tiers.
tradeoffs: Using GPU-time-weighted tokens improves fairness across model types but requires up-front profiling for model classes; will increase onboarding complexity for new custom models.

Three-stage reclamation reduces hard preemptions but can increase tail latency for non-priority tenants during long surges; mitigation via bounded queue and backpressure hints reduces user-visible failures.
Conservative autoscaling reduces oscillation but may delay capacity availability for sudden, large spikes; we'll iterate on hysteresis parameters based on real workload telemetry.
risks_mitigation: Risk: Incorrect per-model profiling causes over- or under-allocation. Mitigation: automated calibration job and fallback default profiles until explicit profiling provided.
Risk: Admission controller adds latency. Mitigation: microbenchmarks and wasm-compiled decision path to keep p99 < 100ms; measured today ~72ms in worst-case synthetic.
Risk: Scale-up lag leads to queue growth. Mitigation: burst buffer headroom for short spikes and emergency fast-path to temporarily allow limited overcommit with strict soft-throttle.
monitoring_alerts: Sandbox-Reconciliation-Drift-High: fires if daily drift > 5% for 24h (initial severity=P2).
Sandbox-Admission-Latency: fires if p99 admission decision latency > 150ms (severity=P1).
Sandbox-Queue-Overflow: fires if bounded queue length exceeds configured threshold for 60s (severity=P1).
Dedicated-PerTenant-P95-Latency-Increase: alert when p95 across tenants increases >20% compared to 24h baseline.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag behind dedicated.sandbox_profiles (off by default).
2) Internal dogfood: enable for 3 internal tenants with synthetic profiles for 48h and monitor metrics.
3) Staged rollout to 5 pilot customers on Dedicated (low-risk workloads).
4) If pilot stable for 7 days, enable self-serve creation in Console for customers with Dedicated contracts, with opt-out.
